matches.description: Watch SC Braga vs Dinamo Minsk highlights and goals from UEFA Europa Conference League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on August 6, 2026. SC Braga and Dinamo Minsk faced off in a highly anticipated UEFA Conference League encounter. Both sides looked to establish their dominance early on in what promised to be a significant night of European football. A Tactical Battle Begins Taking place on August 6, 2026 , the match opened with a physical edge as both teams vied for control of the midfield. Dinamo Minsk displayed a disciplined defensive setup, though their aggression led to an early caution when Fawaz Abdullahi received a yellow card in the 20th minute. SC Braga maintained the majority of possession, patiently probing for a gap in the Belarusian defense that refused to yield easily during the opening exchanges. As the first half progressed, the Portuguese side increased the tempo, forcing the visitors into deeper defensive positions. Despite several promising build-up plays, clear-cut chances remained at a premium until the closing moments of the period. The Breakthrough Before the Break The deadlock was finally broken in the 45th minute following a decisive moment in the penalty area. A lapse in concentration from the Dinamo Minsk defense resulted in a spot-kick being awarded to the hosts. Ricardo Horta stepped up to the mark and clinically dispatched the ball into the net, giving SC Braga a vital lead just seconds before the referee blew for half-time. Second Half Management The second half saw a series of tactical adjustments from both managers. SC Braga introduced Diogo Travassos for Gabriel Silva , while Dinamo Minsk brought on Karen Vardanyan to bolster their attack. The game became increasingly stop-start as substitutions continued, with Demir Tiknaz , Diego Rodrigues , and Fran Navarro all entering the fray for the home side. Discipline became an issue for the visitors as the clock ticked down, with Evgeni Malashevich and Karen Vardanyan both receiving yellow cards. Despite late pressure and the introduction of Gulzhigit Alykulov for the visitors, SC Braga remained composed. The final whistle at 90+3' confirmed a professional performance and a hard-earned result for the Portuguese outfit.
